破例方便了自己时，我仍会思考对别人是否公平。

朋友遇到困难时，我会寻找能替他分担的具体事情。
在新群体里，我常通过照顾他人找到自己的位置。
别人愿意向我求助，会让我感到被需要。
我会把模糊的期待转成能看见成果的目标。
选择任务时，我会考虑它能否展示我的能力。
得到认可后，我常想尽快取得下一个成绩。
即使不流行，我也想保留符合自己感受的风格。
一段经历的情绪层次往往比结果更吸引我。
我希望亲近的人理解我与别人不一样的部分。
面对陌生问题，我想先独自弄懂它的原理。
答应投入项目之前，我会计算它消耗多少精力。
比起立即参与讨论，我更想先掌握足够的信息。
计划有变时，我会先确认谁可以提供可靠支持。
别人说没问题，我仍想知道备用方案是什么。
我需要通过一段时间的实际表现判断能否信任一个人。
行程空出一天，我会兴奋地列出新的玩法。
当事情变得沉闷，我会寻找另一个有趣的切入口。
我喜欢保留多个未来计划，避免生活只有一条路线。
有人替我做重要决定时，我会明确争取决定权。
看到伙伴被不公平对待，我愿意站出来承担压力。
困难局面里，我宁愿直面阻力也不愿被动等待。
群体意见分裂时，我想先找到大家都能接受的部分。
为了保持轻松的相处，我有时会暂缓提出自己的要求。
在紧张场合，我会主动放慢说话节奏缓和气氛。

questions.text: I correct small errors in my work even when nobody checks.
When an exception benefits me, I still consider whether it is fair to others.
An unfair process makes me want to bring it in line with my principles.
When a friend struggles, I look for something concrete I can take off their plate.
In a new group, I often find my place by looking after others.
Being approached for help makes me feel needed.
I turn vague expectations into goals with visible outcomes.
When choosing a task, I consider whether it showcases my abilities.
After recognition, I often want to reach the next milestone quickly.
I keep a style that feels like me even when it is unfashionable.
The emotional layers of an experience often interest me more than its outcome.
I want people close to me to understand what makes me different.
With an unfamiliar problem, I first want to understand its workings alone.
Before joining a project, I consider how much energy it will consume.
I prefer gathering enough information before joining a discussion.
When plans change, I first check who can provide dependable support.
Even when others say it is fine, I want to know the backup plan.
I judge trust through a person’s actions over time.
A free day on a trip makes me excited to list new possibilities.
When something becomes dull, I seek a more interesting angle.
I like keeping several future plans open rather than having one route.
When someone makes an important decision for me, I push for a say.
I am willing to take pressure by speaking up for an unfairly treated teammate.
In a difficult situation, I would rather face resistance than wait passively.
When a group splits, I first look for common ground.
I sometimes delay my own requests to keep interactions relaxed.
In tense situations, I deliberately slow my speech to ease the atmosphere.

dimensions.name: 诚实

dimensions.high: 你目前较常通过谦逊来回应情境：你会承认局限并合理看待贡献。

dimensions.name: 审慎行动

dimensions.high: 你目前较常通过审慎行动来回应情境：你会行动前考虑后果与承诺。

dimensions.name: Creativity
dimensions.low: You rely more on familiar methods and less on recombining resources.
dimensions.high: Creativity is more prominent in your current answers: you try useful new combinations.
dimensions.action: Try a different method for a familiar task and compare results.

dimensions.name: Curiosity
dimensions.low: You explore unfamiliar topics less often, perhaps reserving attention for current priorities.
dimensions.high: Curiosity is more prominent in your current answers: you actively explore unfamiliar information.
dimensions.action: Find two explanations for a recent question.

dimensions.name: Judgment
dimensions.low: You may accept initial judgments quickly; check whether contrary evidence received attention.
dimensions.high: Judgment is more prominent in your current answers: you check evidence and revise views.
dimensions.action: Find one piece of information that could overturn your judgment.

dimensions.name: Love of learning
dimensions.low: You may prefer learning enough for immediate use rather than studying a topic systematically.
dimensions.high: Love of learning is more prominent in your current answers: you systematically develop knowledge and skills.
dimensions.action: Schedule a structured practice session for a topic you want to learn.

dimensions.name: Perspective
dimensions.low: You may focus on immediate details before considering the longer-term or wider context.
dimensions.high: Perspective is more prominent in your current answers: you place problems in a wider context.
dimensions.action: Write one short-term and one long-term view of a concern.

dimensions.name: Bravery
dimensions.low: Voicing dissent may require more safety and support; a low score does not imply a lack of principles.
dimensions.high: Bravery is more prominent in your current answers: you voice important positions despite fear.
dimensions.action: Prepare one clear sentence for a necessary conversation.

dimensions.name: Perseverance
dimensions.low: You may change direction after setbacks; also consider whether the task still merits continuation.
dimensions.high: Perseverance is more prominent in your current answers: you continue meaningful tasks after setbacks.
dimensions.action: Define a next step and a rest boundary for a stalled task.

dimensions.name: Honesty
dimensions.low: Disclosing limits or mistakes may feel uncomfortable; begin with a low-risk factual clarification.
dimensions.high: Honesty is more prominent in your current answers: you align statements with what actually happened.
dimensions.action: Distinguish facts from guesses in one update.

dimensions.name: Zest
dimensions.low: You may currently feel less engaged energy; low energy does not establish a lack of interest.
dimensions.high: Zest is more prominent in your current answers: you participate in daily activities with engagement.
dimensions.action: Engage in one activity for ten minutes and note your energy.

dimensions.name: Love
dimensions.low: Expressing closeness or accepting care may need more trust; this does not imply an inability to love.
dimensions.high: Love is more prominent in your current answers: you build mutually caring close connections.
dimensions.action: Express one specific form of care to someone you trust.

dimensions.name: Kindness
dimensions.low: You offer help less spontaneously, perhaps protecting limited time and energy.
dimensions.high: Kindness is more prominent in your current answers: you respond to others' concrete difficulties.
dimensions.action: Ask someone what help they actually need.

dimensions.name: Social intelligence
dimensions.low: You may rely on explicit language and adjust less to silence, tone or other interaction cues.
dimensions.high: Social intelligence is more prominent in your current answers: you notice feelings and cues in interactions.
dimensions.action: Turn a guess about someone's feelings into a gentle check.

dimensions.name: Teamwork
dimensions.low: You may prefer working independently and need clearer responsibilities to engage in shared work.
dimensions.high: Teamwork is more prominent in your current answers: you take responsibility in shared work.
dimensions.action: Confirm one team commitment and the help it requires.

dimensions.name: Fairness
dimensions.low: You check allocation criteria less often; notice whether familiarity influences opportunities.
dimensions.high: Fairness is more prominent in your current answers: you allocate opportunities using consistent principles.
dimensions.action: Check whether an allocation rule gives everyone a voice.

dimensions.name: Leadership
dimensions.low: You may prefer contributing as a participant to organizing goals, responsibilities and follow-through.
dimensions.high: Leadership is more prominent in your current answers: you organize participation toward shared goals.
dimensions.action: Clarify a shared task's next step, owner and feedback time.

dimensions.name: Forgiveness
dimensions.low: After hurt, you may need more time or distance; forgiveness need not remove safety boundaries.
dimensions.high: Forgiveness is more prominent in your current answers: you allow repair within appropriate boundaries.
dimensions.action: Separate releasing resentment from conditions for rebuilding trust.

dimensions.name: Humility
dimensions.low: You may emphasize your own contribution and judgment; check whether others receive room and credit.
dimensions.high: Humility is more prominent in your current answers: you acknowledge limits and put contributions in proportion.
dimensions.action: Ask a peer to identify a limitation you have missed.

dimensions.name: Prudence
dimensions.low: You may commit or respond quickly; hard-to-reverse decisions merit another consequence check.
dimensions.high: Prudence is more prominent in your current answers: you consider consequences and commitments before acting.
dimensions.action: Leave time to reconsider one impulsive decision.

dimensions.name: Self-regulation
dimensions.low: Distractions and interruptions may disrupt plans; environmental support may help.
dimensions.high: Self-regulation is more prominent in your current answers: you support personal plans and routines.
dimensions.action: Set a practical environmental limit on one distraction.

dimensions.name: Appreciation of beauty and excellence
dimensions.low: You pause less often to appreciate nature, crafted work or skill; attention and opportunity also affect answers.
dimensions.high: Appreciation of beauty and excellence is more prominent in your current answers: you notice beauty in nature, art and skill.
dimensions.action: Record one instance of beauty or skill that made you pause.

dimensions.name: Gratitude
dimensions.low: You reflect on or express received support less often; this does not mean support is absent.
dimensions.high: Gratitude is more prominent in your current answers: you notice support received and express thanks.
dimensions.action: Tell someone who helped you exactly what difference it made.

dimensions.name: Hope
dimensions.low: Finding future paths may currently feel difficult; start with one small controllable step.
dimensions.high: Hope is more prominent in your current answers: you seek feasible future paths through difficulty.
dimensions.action: Write two paths toward a wish and one controllable starting point.

dimensions.name: Humor
dimensions.low: You may respond more seriously and directly; humor is not required for successful interaction.
dimensions.high: Humor is more prominent in your current answers: you respond with considerate lightness.
dimensions.action: Try a lighthearted remark that does not target someone else.

dimensions.name: Meaning and spirituality
dimensions.low: You draw less on larger beliefs or spiritual connections; meaning can also come through concrete relationships and actions.
dimensions.high: Meaning and spirituality is more prominent in your current answers: you understand life through beliefs or larger purposes.
dimensions.action: Write the value or belief connected to one daily choice.

questions.text: When old tools fail, I recombine materials at hand.
When planning an activity, I enjoy suggesting an untried format.
I modify existing methods to fit new constraints.
When encountering an unfamiliar topic, I want to understand why it matters.
In an unfamiliar place, I notice details distinctive to it.
When I hear about an unexpected phenomenon, I ask why it happens.
I check the source even when a claim supports my view.
When new evidence conflicts with my judgment, I reassess it.
In a disagreement, I try to articulate the other side's reasoning fully.
After learning basic operations, I still want to understand the principles.
I keep studying a topic even without an exam requirement.
When learning a skill, I organize scattered knowledge into a structure.
When a friend seeks advice, I consider immediate difficulties and longer-term needs.
For complex choices, I connect lessons from different past experiences.
I can help people in a discussion see the wider context they overlooked.
Even if unwelcome, I am willing to point out a safety concern.
When someone is treated unfairly, I am willing to object.
Despite fearing embarrassment, I ask questions that help the situation.
After a first failure on an important task, I adjust my approach and continue.
When progress is not visible, I still complete planned practice.
For tedious but necessary finishing work, I find a way to complete it.
I acknowledge my part in a shared mistake.
When I do not know an answer, I am willing to say so.
When presenting work, I explain which parts came from others' help.
When starting an activity I value, I often feel eager to engage.
Even in a familiar activity, I find something to engage with.
When I have energy, I participate actively rather than only observe.
I let people close to me know they matter to me.
When I need support, I can accept care from people I trust.
When someone close shares good news, I celebrate attentively with them.
When someone is overwhelmed, I ask whether I can help with one small task.
When helping, I consider whether the person wants to receive it.
Even without a return, I offer help within my capacity.
When someone goes quiet, I consider whether the topic needs changing.
When the same words affect people differently, I try to understand why.
In a new group, I observe how people express agreement and dissatisfaction.
After dividing team work, I complete my agreed part.
When shared work stalls, I coordinate instead of focusing only on my progress.
When a member cannot participate, I discuss redistributing the work.
When allocating opportunities, I check whether I favor familiar people.
When assessing others' actions, I try to use consistent criteria.
When resources are limited, I explain the allocation criteria.
When a team lacks a next step, I help clarify the goal.
When organizing activities, I consider how different members can participate.
After a shared decision, I help confirm who will carry it out.
After a sincere apology for a minor mistake, I allow a chance to improve.
After resolving a disagreement, I try not to use the past as a weapon.
After an offense, I can consider context while keeping my boundaries.
When shared work is praised, I mention others' contributions.
When someone understands a problem better, I ask for their guidance.
When my judgment is wrong, I acknowledge the need to improve.
Before a hard-to-reverse commitment, I examine consequences.
When emotions are strong, I delay sending potentially hurtful messages.
Before accepting extra work, I check whether I can deliver.
When I want to finish a task, I reduce likely distractions.
When a habit is interrupted, I schedule a return to it.
When I want immediate gratification, I can pause to consider my plan.
When I see carefully made work, I notice its details.
On everyday journeys, a natural scene can make me pause to appreciate it.
Seeing someone skillfully perform complex work can inspire admiration.
When someone makes an extra effort for me, I notice it.
Looking back on a day, I can identify small things I appreciate.
After receiving help, I tell the person what it meant to me.
When a plan fails, I can still imagine ways forward.
Facing an uncertain future, I look for one step I can take.
When one route is blocked, I look for other feasible paths.
When things feel tense, I look for a lighthearted expression that hurts no one.
In a minor awkward moment, I can sometimes see the funny side.
With familiar people, I enjoy sharing observations that make us smile.
For major choices, I consult my understanding of life's meaning.
Certain rituals, reflection or beliefs help me keep an inner direction.
Thinking about my connection with a larger community or world gives me meaning.

dimensions.name: 诚实谦逊
dimensions.low: 你的回答较少强调主动披露利益和分享功劳；这不能据此判断道德品质。

dimensions.action: 为一件担忧写下可求助的人和具体请求。

dimensions.name: 互动活力

dimensions.action: 尝试一次短发言，记录互动前后的精力。

dimensions.name: 宽和耐心

dimensions.high: 你目前较常通过宽和耐心来回应情境：你愿意给失误者解释与修复的机会。
dimensions.action: 针对一次小摩擦提出具体修复办法。

dimensions.name: 有序落实
dimensions.low: 你可能偏好灵活安排，但重要交付仍可借助少量检查点。

questions.text: When a task feels boring, I keep finding other little things to do.
Thinking about an uncomfortable email makes me want to open it later.
Even when something is not hard, tedious steps can make me leave it until the end.
When I cannot ensure a good opening, I delay writing.
Imagining criticism makes me prepare repeatedly without submitting.
If the result may miss my standards, I sometimes prefer not to start yet.
With many ways to begin, I often compare too long without acting.
When I do not know the first step, I set the whole task aside.
I delay more when I must define the task’s completion criteria myself.

questions.text: For important options, I list evidence and uncertainties.
Even when a recommendation appeals to me, I want its data source.
Before choosing, I check whether unlike criteria are being mixed together.
In familiar situations, I often quickly sense which choice fits.
Sometimes I form an overall judgment before checking specific reasons.
Past experience gives me an immediate sense of trust or doubt about some options.
Before an important decision, I consider whether I can bear the worst case.
For long-term commitments, I examine exit conditions carefully.
When information is limited, I prefer leaving myself a buffer.
When unsure about a new method, I am willing to try it on a small scale.
For two low-risk options, I prefer gaining information through experience.
I adjust later choices based on the result of a short trial.
